data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's booked gross claims reserves opened at GBP 144.225m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates a net favourable prior-year release of approximately GBP 16.2m (11.2% of opening reserves) driven by favourable development on several older underwriting years, partly offset by adverse developments attributable to major loss events (notably Covid-related contingency exposures and certain property catastrophe losses). The most material specific prior-year reserve movements highlighted were an GBP 8.2m increase in COVID-related reserves and adverse development related to the Iowa derecho, with most large current-year catastrophe impacts allocated across property/reinsurance accounts.
raw_causal_phrases: losses from the 2020 underwriting year. The key drivers of these losses in the year, included winter storm Uri (GBP 12.9 million), hurricane Ida (GBP 1.8 million), Measat (GBP 0.4 million) and adverse development on 2020 losses, including covid losses (GBP 8.2 million) and the Iowa derecho (GBP 2.3 million).

There was an increase in prior year reserves including a GBP 8.2 million increase on the COVID loss reserves, which are now at GBP 19.1 million (2020: GBP 10.9 million) gross of reinsurance and GBP 19.1 million (2020: GBP 9.8 million) net of reinsurance.
The 2021 result for the 2020 and prior underwriting years in calendar year 2021 was a loss of GBP 16.1 million.
data.data_quality_notes: Calculated prior-year gross movement based on the gross claims development triangle (page 39). There is an inconsistency between net prior-year result language (net loss of GBP 16.1m on 2020 & prior YOAs) and the gross triangle-derived PYD (a net gross release of ~GBP 16.186m). The notable catastrophe table shows gross adverse impacts allocated to 2020 & prior YOAs of GBP 39.8m (gross). The triangle and movement results therefore present a mixed picture (releases in older years offset by large 2021-allocated adverse prior-year impacts). Minor mismatches exist between divisional premium totals and P&L totals; percentages are computed against the P&L gross premium written figure.
